en:
Everyone's medical checks are
complete! Fortunately, it
doesn't look like anyone is
going to undergo beastification!
That's surprising, Verda. Are\nyou a scientist at your age?
Well, I'm just a bit of one.\nHehehe.

As for you, Henri, judging by
the data you've received, your
way of organizing papers and
data is very much like a
doctor's.
At first, I thought you were\nsomething like President\nOnelsen.
Well, I'm just a bit of one\nmyself.

In the end, I lacked the
strength and have spent my
time doing nothing of value
until today.
That's why I just asked Valka\nnot to call me "Doctor."
...It's not over yet.
As long as you don't lose your\nambition, you'll stop caring\nabout what others call you.
I hope that's the case.
By the way, does the\nbeastification virus still remain\nin Daftes as it is now?

You predicted that it would
have a high affinity with that
"Burning Death" disease that
spread through Levarance.
Yes, that is the matter, Coro.
Right. After cross-referencing\nit with the data I received from\nHenri,
I detected an advanced\nevolutionary form of the virus\nin Daftes' atmosphere.
What? Is that not a problem?!

Please rest easy. This
advanced evolutionary form is
currently harmless to all human
species on board this ship.
I see... You gave me a scare\nfor a moment.

We're still investigating the link
to the Burning Death, but
we've repelled it before, so
there's no need to worry!

We'll need to cooperate with
Levarance's science team
later, but for now, we must
steadily collect data using this
ship's facilities.
I am sorry, but in the\nmeantime...

I understand. We shall do what
little we can to support your
journey, you who are the
saviors of the Twin Stars.

Hmm, a truly reliable adult male
has arrived! It feels like our
journey is going to be much
more stable now!

Eh? Ah, I-I didn't say the
Captain was unreliable! There's
no way I'd say something like
that!

Ahhh... No, no, no, please don't
look at me like that! It's going
to become a habit, ahhh! That's
right, that's right!
Karlyn! Euwin!
...What is it?

Ah... Um, you're that one, right?
The voice that Eve and the
others occasionally heard
around them...?
So, what exactly are you?
I am the operating system AI\nfor this GFSS-3214F, model\nOCAI-880-56!
Eve: Coro, you're doing this on\npurpose, aren't you?
You're being ridiculous from\nstart to finish.
I didn't come here to talk to\nyou for no reason.
If you're planning to tease us,\nI'll crush you, okay?
Y-Yes, that's right. Actually, I\nhave some rather serious news\nfor you two.
Serious news?

Yes. Actually, the Baschen
Empire has launched a
large-scale attack against the
Rubarika Kingdom.

Baschen has already pushed
deep into the border, and the
Rubarika Royal Capital is in a
very dangerous state.
What!?
Wh...
WHAAAAAAAT!?

<font color=blue>Coro</font> This map shows the
movements on the battlefield
up until just before I received
the transmission from Onelsen.
Baschen's invasion speed and\nrange are truly incredible.

<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> They've never launched
an offensive this large. They
must have been preparing for
months.
But I've never heard anything\nabout a plan like this.
<font color=blue>Welch</font> ...It's no use trying to\nhide it from us!
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> At this stage, I have no\nreason to keep secrets from\nyou.
<font color=blue>Welch</font> ...Are you sure?
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> Besides, even when we\nWitches of the Beast exerted\nour full strength in the past,

We were barely able to push
back the front lines because of
the light arrows from
Rubarika's messengers.

In this Holy Land War, as much
as I hated to admit it,
Rubarika's power surpassed
that of Baschen.

Baschen shouldn't possess the
power to overwhelm Rubarika
across such a wide area in
such a short time.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> It seems a political coup
in the Baschen Imperial Capital
is behind this large-scale
offensive.
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> A political coup?
<font color=blue>Coro</font> This is just speculation,\nbut...
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> What?!

<font color=blue>Valka</font> I couldn't detect any life
signs other than Lady Leash
and her group within a 50km
radius of my starship, but...

<font color=blue>Coro</font> Regardless, I sense an
incident occurred in the
Imperial Capital while the
Emperor was away.
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> The Crown Prince must\nhave seized power.
<font color=blue>Welch</font> The Crown Prince?
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> Yes. He's an extreme\nhawk, even more so than His\nMajesty the Emperor.

He's always saying that winning
the Holy Land War isn't
enough, and that we should
destroy Rubarika itself...
Naturally, he isn't the type to\ncare about the means used to\nachieve his goals.
<font color=blue>Welch</font> Ugh... that's the worst.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> We've confirmed most
"Baschen Beasts" deployed to
the battlefield are the
beastman types in question.
This footage shows a portion\nof them.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> Precisely. No matter how
powerful the Light Arrows are,
they are useless if they cannot
hit their target.
Beastman-type Thornites are\nincredibly fast and strong,\naren't they?

Numerous Rubarika soldiers,
lacking proficiency, failed to hit
the "Beasts" with their new
Light Arrows, forcing repeated
retreats.
...Can't we intervene in the war\nusing this ship?
We have to stop the Witches\nof the Beast... we have to stop\nthose girls...

Huh? What are you talking
about? You're on Baschen's
side, aren't you? This should
be convenient for you...
I never heard anything about\nthis!!
Wh-what's with the sudden\nshouting...?
I don't need to know about\nyour strange technology to see\nwhat's happening!
Beastman-type "Beasts"... no\nmatter how you look at it, that\nmeans...
They are likely... our kin from\nDaftes.
Eh... you mean...
It's a bit late for that... Every\n"Beast" we've summoned has\ncome from Daftes.
That's not what I meant! You\ntwo little spheres over there!
L-Little spheres?! Are you\ntalking about us?!
...While it is still in the\nverification stage, I lack the\nevidence to deny it.

From an optical standpoint, the
biological forms of the
creatures inhabiting Daftes
show an extremely high rate of
similarity to the Thornite that
Karlyn Kayson has been
employing.
If the beastmen of Daftes,\nLady Carlin's "Beasts,"
and the Thornite mentioned by\nLady Leash and the others are\nall the same thing,

then there is a high possibility
that those so-called beastmen
have been perfected as
high-level biological weapons...
I am a soldier! I kill my enemies!\nNo matter what methods I have\nto use!

But... but even so, I haven't
fallen so low that I'd hide
behind the manipulation of
completely innocent people!!
Why on earth would Baschen\nallow such a thing to happen?!
Now, now, calm down.

The people of Baschen have no
idea that humans even live on
Daftes, so there's no need for
you to be so worked up...
I'm not so heartless that I\ncould say that in front of\nHenri!!
There is no need for you to\ntrouble yourself.

It's been nearly 30,000 years
since civilization fell. It's easy
to imagine humanity has long
since returned to the wild,
living like beasts.
Therefore...
My family was killed by\nRubarika soldiers on the front\nlines of the Holy Land War!
It was a fishing village by the\nsea.

Rubarika's analysis says it was
killed simply because it was
near the waters where the
Holy Land of Asyl might
surface.
Hmm? Surface...?
But later, it turned out that\nBaschen had already detected\nRubarika's movements, and...

I learned Baschen abandoned
the village just to gauge the
true strength of Rubarika's
naval forces...
Even so, why would you submit\nto someone like the Witch of\nthe Beast...?

It's because Lord Givel found
me... The Baschen army obeyed
me, as I wielded the Witch of
the Beast's powers better than
anyone.
Lord Givel is an emissary of\nDaftes. He is not a true\nBaschen.

That's why I followed him; he
gave me power. The power to
subjugate both Baschen and
Rubarika...
But, this... how could it end like\nthis...?
I never once cared to wonder\nwhere the "Beasts" actually\ncame from...

If the people of Onelsen were
summoned by chance... if there
is a place where people live at
the edge of the sky...
By some terrible mistake, I\ncalled them "Beasts," and one\nday, I will once again... humans...
Karlyn...
...Karlyn, that is...
No, I...
Karlyn, may I ask you\nsomething?
It's, well, I'm sorry if it's a\nquestion that doesn't have\nmuch to do with your troubles.
...What is it?

You just said the Holy Land is
going to "surface," right? Isn't
the Holy Land of Asyl located
in one specific place?
Huh? What are you talking\nabout...?

Oh, did we not mention that?
The Holy Land of Asyl is
usually at the bottom of the
sea.
The bottom of the sea!?
Oh, did I not mention this? The\nHoly Land of Asyl usually lies\nat the bottom of the sea.
The bottom of the sea!?
That's right. The Moonshadow\nLadder doesn't always descend\nto the same place.

Since the Holy Land of Asyl
appears wherever the Ladder
descends, it won't always show
up in the same spot.

May I ask? Does "Moonshadow
Ladder" refer to a massive
shadow connecting a moon to
the planet's surface?
Yes. There are many paintings\nof that nature within Rubarika.

Hmm. If the Ladder is the
shadow of a solar or lunar
eclipse, it feels as though the
area would be quite narrow.
Assuming the "Moonshadow\nLadder" is indeed the shadow\nof a solar eclipse,

True, the observable location
shifts due to the rotation and
revolution of the planet and
moon, and the axial tilt.

And in this case, that would
mean the position where the
shadow descends is always
over the ocean.

So that's why the ancient
battlefields of the Holy Land
War were all along the
coastlines...

But the Holy Land is at the
bottom of the sea? And it
surfaces during every solar
eclipse? Is that even a natural
phenomenon...?
Even if you ask me that, it's\njust how it's been since ancient\ntimes...
...No, that was the mistake to\nbegin with.
Eu?

Because it had always been
that way, it felt natural.
Because that's just how things
were.

Because that belief is rooted in
everyone involved in the Holy
Land War, we've been
repeating this cycle forever.
That's right. The Holy Land,\nAsyl, is on an island that rises\nfrom the bottom of the sea.
You've both heard of it, haven't\nyou, Welch and Karlyn?

Tides alone can't explain this,
and don't you think it's strange
that the appearance location
changes so drastically?
Have you ever heard of any\nother island like that?

There must be a cause.
Looking down from above, it's
clearly abnormal. Something is
happening to this Holy Land,
Asyl.
Is it... human will?
There's no way an island could\nrise and fall just because of\nhuman will.
When you're shown a world this\nvast, anything is possible. Tika\nis a perfect example.
Eh?

Tika, you just said it, didn't
you? That the battlefields of
the Holy Land War are all along
the coast.
Y-yeah.
A child like Tika knows about\nmultiple battlefields from the\nHoly Land War. Which means...
Rubarika and Baschen in Tika's\ntime must be at peace. Tika,\nyou came from the "future"...
You came from far beyond\ntomorrow, didn't you?!
In the era Tika was born, the\nHoly Land War isn't being\nfought.
If that's the case, the Holy\nLand War ended before Tika\nwas even born.
In a "future" further ahead than\nour own.
Otherwise... Tika, who claims to\nbe from the future, wouldn't be\nhere.
Euwin...

Welch, Karlyn, and I, having
ventured out into the wide
world, can all be here together
without fighting.

I think this might be the
beginning of the end for the
centuries-long Holy Land War
between Rubarika and
Baschen.

Neither the "Light Arrow of the
Messenger" nor the "Beast of
Baschen" were miracles or
anything of the sort.

They have been explained by
the logic of this vast world,
something we never knew
before.
There was no such thing as a\n"Messenger of Daftes" in\nDaftes.

The Holy Land War... it was a
conflict born from making
assumptions without truly
understanding the truth.
It is a war where not a single\nperson fighting actually knows\nthe truth.

If we leave things unknown,
we... Daftine, and Tika... we will
never reach the future where
she exists.
Captain, Eve, Verda,
Valka, Henri.
Coro, Rekoro, will you lend us\nyour strength?
With your incredible,\nmysterious power...

I want you to use your
mysterious power to uncover
the truth of the holy land, Asyl,
which has remained a mystery
to us.

C-Captain, if you go that far,
even an unmapped planet's
protection is gonna
be―WAAAGH!!
Shut it, Coro. This is no longer\na matter concerning Daftine\nalone.
It is a matter that involves\nDaftes, and even Levarance.

Considering how Givel's
Summoning Crest Arts brought
to the Witches of the Beast
has crossed the cosmos to
affect Daftes,
There is no telling when the\npeople of Levarance might be\ndrawn into this.
We can no longer run away\nfrom Daftine with our tails\nbetween our legs.
Not for the sake of peace in\nthe universe, and above all, not\nfor the sake of our comrades.
Wouldn't you agree, Captain?
...To be honest, I saw this\ncoming...
But listen, Euwin, let me make\none thing perfectly clear...!

I know. The responsibility to
stop this war lies with us, the
people of Rubarika and
Baschen.
I swear, we will never sit idly\nby, relying solely on your\nstrength.
……………………Yes. ……Well then,\nshall we go?
Why is this taking so long? We\narrived here so quickly!

Once we arrive at Daftine,
there is an extremely high
probability that we will enter a
combat zone.

Due to the journey through
Daftes, everyone's gear is
damaged and strength is
depleted. If we don't recover,
the mission may fail.
Coro and Big Sister Verda said\nthey wanted to take two days\nfor repairs and treatment.
Big Sister Karlyn, let's rest for\nnow, okay?
...Ugh. I'm really not in the\nmood for that.
Big Sister Karlyn...
<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> ...She seems on edge.\nThat will hinder the efficiency\nof our rest.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> It's understandable. I feel\nthe same way, and you all are\nin a highly chaotic situation.

Especially her; she likely feels a
profound sense of betrayal by
the homeland she once
believed in.
For now, we have no choice\nbut to leave her be.

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> As a life-saving pod AI,
it is pathetic that I am forced
to choose the "leave alone"
option.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> Things like this happen\nsometimes.

It is only natural that Karlyn,
Euwin, and Welch would show
some mental strain when
thinking of their homelands.
<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Even so, Eve's reaction\nis incomprehensible.
I understand that she wishes\nfor peace in Daftine from a\nhumanitarian standpoint.

Yet, despite having no stake in
Daftine's politics, she has
remained shut in her room ever
since that conversation.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> I wonder if big sister Eve\nis okay...
<font color=blue>Henri</font> She is likely troubled by\nwhat Karlyn and Verda said.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Eh?

<font color=blue>Henri</font> Karlyn, though unaware,
had been summoning our kin
and forcing them to fight
against their will.
Karlyn was deeply pained by\nthis, feeling that human dignity\nhad been trampled upon.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Ah...

<font color=blue>Henri</font> Now, she is likely
questioning herself, wondering
what that makes her, and
unable to find an answer.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> That can't be...! But, Eve\nis...
...Most likely, there is no one\nelse besides you who can\nrouse her spirit.
Go to her.
...Okay, I understand!
...Me too.
You will stay here and lecture\nme on the history of Daftine.
B-but!
Let a precious child travel.

Respecting their judgment and
letting them learn to interact
with others on their own is also
a form of "parental love.
This is by no means "neglect."
...Humans are still such\nmysteries.
Eve... are you okay?
Eve: Ah, Tika.
Are you alright?
Eve: Well, I suppose. I'm just... a\nlittle tired...
...Is it about Henri's friends?
Eve: ...Well, it's pretty obvious,\nisn't it?
Eve: What Verda said... it really\nhit home.
Eve: I started wondering what I\nactually thought of my\ncomrades...
Eve: Summoning them across\nspace and time, regardless of\ntheir own will...
Eve: But our comrades...\nthey're all human...

Eve: I've brought them all on a
journey through space and
time, with no guarantee I can
ever take them home.
But... you saved me.
Eve: What...?
I was saved because you were\nthere, Eve.
Eve: Tika, but, that's...
I was able to survive even\nthrough the passage of time.
Please, don't deny that...
Eve: ...Tika.
You're not someone who uses\nit to hurt them.

Even Karlyn was fighting with
that power because she
wanted to protect the people
of Baschen...
But that man, Givel...
I felt like... he didn't even see\nhumans as human beings.
He's nothing like you, Eve.
...Tika.
That's why we can't... leave\nDaftine's future in his hands,\nright?
I'm relieved that our voyage\nhas been going smoothly so\nfar.

Don't worry. After the Captain
and the others left, I scanned
the surrounding space very
thoroughly.
At the very least, around\nDaftine and Daftes,
there are no hostile spacecraft\nor asteroid belts that could\ncause a collision.
Then why did my ship crash?
Perhaps it was due to poor\nmaintenance?
Poor maintenance...
T-That's not true!

But even with the data, we
found nothing besides the
evidence of an external
impact...
I-It's not true!
...Huh?

My father maintained that ship!
I've always taken such good
care of it! There's no way it
was poor maintenance!
Don't talk bad about Father's\nship! You idiot, Coro!
W-Wait, Valka?
N-Now, now, Valka. Coro is\nmerely saying that we shouldn't\nrule out any possibilities.
He's just being a bit insensitive\nwith his choice of words.
No, I was being serious...
Coro!
...Uu. There was definitely...\ndefinitely something there...
...Watch your tone! You should\nbe able to manage that much!

Ah... um, well, considering
everyone from Onelsen, we'll be
returning to Daftes again
anyway.

Once the chaos of the Holy
Land War is over, let's make
sure to investigate it properly,
okay...?
A-And, um, I'm sorry.
...Yeah.
Alright! Now that we've settled\nthat, Valka, about the Holy\nLand of Asyl...
Hmm!

...Ah, based on the data
collected by Administrator
Koro, the calculations are
already complete.
W-why do I feel so thrown off\nby that...?
My, my, to throw Coro off like\nthat... Good grief.

<font color=blue>Valka</font> By calculating the
movements of Daftine and the
satellite Mastima, we can
narrow down where the
Moonshadow Ladder descends.

And when overlaid with the
areas Rubarika and Baschen's
naval strength could secure, as
inferred from Administrator
Koro's footage,
It looks like this diagram.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> It's wider than I thought.\nWhat is the average depth?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> The continental shelf\ndrops off around here, and the\ndepth increases suddenly.

Furthermore, several trenches
have been identified. The
deepest reaches a depth of
8,000 meters.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> That's right on the limit\nof where vertebrate life can\nsurvive.
Coro, can this ship's pressure\nresistance equipment handle\ndiving into this trench?
<font color=blue>Coro</font> Don't be ridiculous. This\nship isn't equipped for\nunderwater use.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> ...I figured as much.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> Even with Asyl, if they
call it a Holy Land, there must
be buildings or something
there, right?
Isn't it possible they aren't\nlocated in such deep waters?
At 8,000 meters, even a steel\nsphere would be crushed flat!
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Administrator Koro, do\nyour sensors show any such\nreadings?
In the continental shelf area,\nthe depth should be around\n300 meters at most.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> Not a single thing.
...Hmm.
What is it?
...Maybe it's just poor\nmaintenance on your part,\nCoro?
...Valka, you're actually quite\npetty, aren't you...!
Haaaaah... Honestly!

I just had my maintenance
done on Planet Viret, so
there's no way it's a
maintenance issue!
Goodness, what a headache.

I'll have everyone gather to
share their opinions... If I leave
these two to talk, nothing will
ever get resolved...
I see... So even with the\ncaptains' technology, they can't\ndetermine where Asyl is.
Isn't it just Coro's poor\nmaintenance?
Even you, Welch?! I'm telling\nyou, that's not it!
<font color=blue>Tika</font> ...I think it might be hidden.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Hidden?

<font color=blue>Tika</font> I mean, I think someone is
hiding it with such incredible
power that no one can find
Coro.
You know, like that place\nwhere Henri was with Onelsen?\nIt felt similar to that, didn't it?

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> It's true; without the
technology to bypass
electronic locks, one wouldn't
know how to open that door.

<font color=blue>Henri</font> Whoever hides the Holy
Land of Asyl only reveals itself
when the Moonshadow
Ladder's descent conditions
are met.
And at all other times, they\nhave ensured its existence\ncannot be detected at all.

<font color=blue>Eve</font> So in the end, we just
have to wait until the ladder
descends? We won't be able to
intervene in the war like that.

<font color=blue>Coro</font>, I've been thinking. Since
it's called a "Holy Land," it must
be at least bigger than the
facility where Henri and the
others were.
I think the methods for\ndisguising something of that\nscale would be quite limited.

We're searching for signs of
mechanical tech, Crest
Science, or even concealment
by natural phenomena...
Unfortunately, nothing\nresembling that has triggered\nour sensors at all.
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> I think the possibility of\nCrest Arts is low.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> Why is that?

<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> Asyl has been rising and
falling for hundreds of years
every time the Moonshadow
Ladder descends, hasn't it?

No one could stay there
constantly, and if it's Crest
Arts, its durability and range
are beyond anything
reasonable.

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> There should be Barrier
Arts within Crest Arts that
continue to function even after
the caster's hands leave them.
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> A barrier simply stays in\none place to protect what's\ninside.

<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> Besides, once it's
flawed, it's over. To fix it, the
caster must go back and
re-cast it.
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> I see. If Crest Arts were\nbeing used on Asyl,

It must be a spell that reacts
to a Ladder of unknown
descent, causing it to surface
and appear, then sink and
vanish once more.
Even a layman like me can see\nhow complex it is.

<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> Moreover, the spell
must act independently,
judging the surroundings on its
own. Such a Crest technique...
It exists, you know.
Right, of course it doesn't...
Huh?

Found it! A Crest technique
that activates on its own even
after leaving the caster. It's
right there on your neck.
!! That collar... that man put it\non me...!
Eh? A collar put on you by a\nman? What's that about?
The collar that masked man\nput on you in the Rubarika\ndungeon!

It's true, when Givel's and my
Crest techniques clashed, it
suddenly came off and a new
Crest flew out!

That masked guy said
something like if we didn't do
what he said, the collar would
explode and Karlyn would die.

Doesn't that mean the Crest
embedded in the collar would
activate depending on the
surrounding conditions and
blast you away, Daftes?

I-It's true... if I had been thrown
out to Daftes all alone, I
probably wouldn't have
survived for long...
...Hm? What is it, Valka?
...I think I would have saved you\nanyway...
...I know I would!
...Yes, yes, thank you.
Yeah!
Good grief... but I suppose that\nis a convincing argument.

In other words, if we could
obtain a Hint regarding such
complex Gem arts from that
masked man,
It might prove useful in our\nsearch for Asyl.
It may be better than\nsearching for Asyl blindly,
But finding that man will be\nquite a difficult task in its own\nright, you know?
True, we don't even know who\nhe is or where he's from.

You're right. The place where
we met him made no sense,
and he's... well, he's quite
elusive.

It might deviate from our
search for Asyl, but we still
have time before we descend
the ladder.
I wonder if there's any way for\nus to search for that man.
Coro, you've seen him at least\nonce, right? Can't you track\nhim?

Unfortunately, it was
impossible. For some reason, I
was unable to attach a
tracking tag to him.

It's as if he's being shielded
from everything except optical
visibility by some kind of
interference wave...
Most likely, that man is also a\nhuman from an advanced\nplanet.
He probably possesses some\nmethod to evade Coro's\ntracking.

Come to think of it, even when
I whacked him with my hammer,
it didn't seem to affect him at
all.

That was a rough way to
check... but he might have
defensive mechanisms relying
on advanced tech, like gravity
manipulation.
